findings.title: Backup code can bypass password verification with a dummy TOTP field
findings.body: Password verification is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is non-empty, without exempting the new backup-code path. An attacker calling the credentials endpoint directly with a valid backup code, any non-empty totpCode value, and no/wrong password therefore skips verifyPassword, then enters the backupCode branch (which never validates the dummy totpCode) and is authenticated. A backup code, intended only as a second factor, becomes a single-factor passwordless login credential.

findings.title: Single-use backup codes can be replayed concurrently
findings.body: Consumption is a non-atomic read-check-update: two simultaneous logins with the same backup code can both read the stored array, both find the code at the same index, and both authenticate before either request writes back the array with that entry nulled. The documented 'exactly once' property of backup codes is therefore not enforced under concurrent requests; the code should be consumed with an atomic/conditional update or lock.

findings.title: Backup code comparison does not normalize letter case
findings.body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex')) and the only normalization applied to user input is stripping '-'. A user who types or pastes their code in uppercase (a natural way to transcribe XXXXX-XXXXX codes) gets IncorrectBackupCode even though the code is correct. The same flaw exists in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61. Input should be lowercased (and trimmed) before comparison in both places.

findings.title: Backup codes are persisted and returned before TOTP setup is verified
findings.body: Setup writes the encrypted backup codes (and TOTP secret) to the user row and returns the plaintext codes in the setup response before the user has proven possession of the authenticator by completing the enable step. If setup is abandoned, valid backup codes for a not-yet-enabled account remain stored in the database, and the codes are already exposed to any client/script that called setup, even though the UI only displays them after enabling. Codes should be generated/confirmed at enable time, or at minimum not persisted until enable succeeds.

findings.title: No test exercises logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The new e2e coverage only downloads/copies the codes during setup; the file itself notes 'TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. The security-critical behaviors added in this PR — login with a backup code, rejection of a wrong code, single-use invalidation on reuse, missing-codes handling for pre-existing 2FA users, and disabling 2FA with a backup code — have no automated verification, so regressions or bypasses in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts would ship undetected.
